subject: health
title: Good Manners
about: Excuse me, waiting for a turn to talk, listening with eyes and a quiet mouth, napkin on the lap, chewing with a closed mouth, asking to be excused, giving people room, holding the door, greeting people, a library voice, and making things right after sorry. NC 1.ICHR.1.1 (respect personal space and boundaries) and 1.MEH.1.1 (good ways to ask for what you need) plus PE.1.PR.4.1 (listen and follow directions); builds on Good Friends and Kind Words with new situations.
tip: Pick one manner for the week, like napkin on lap or excuse me, and cheer every time he remembers it on his own.

cards.q: You burp at the table. What do you say?
cards.note: Everyone burps sometimes. A quick excuse me is all it takes.

cards.q: Two kids are standing in your way in the hall. What do you say to get by?
cards.note: Say excuse me, then wait a moment for them to make room.

cards.q: Two grown-ups are talking. You want to tell them about your day. What do you do?
cards.note: Put a hand gently on your grown-up's arm and wait. If it really cannot wait, say excuse me.

cards.q: Your teacher is talking to the class. Where do your eyes go?
cards.note: Listening with your eyes shows the teacher you are ready to learn.

cards.q: A friend is telling you a story. What does a good listener do?
cards.note: Eyes on the talker, mouth quiet, body still. That is whole-body listening.

cards.q: Where does your napkin go while you eat?
cards.note: Use it to wipe your mouth and fingers, then put it back on your lap.

cards.q: Your mouth is full of food. When is it polite to talk?
cards.note: Chew, swallow, then talk. No one wants to see your food.

cards.q: How do you chew your food at the table?
cards.note: Small bites make it easier to chew with your mouth closed.

cards.q: The peas are across the table. What is the polite thing to say?
cards.note: Asking someone to pass a dish keeps elbows out of the food.

cards.q: You are done eating. What do you ask before you leave the table?
cards.note: Ask, wait for a yes, then carry your plate to the sink.

cards.q: A friend takes a step back while you talk. What does that tell you?
cards.note: About an arm's length apart is a good talking distance.

cards.q: You open a door and someone is right behind you. What can you do?
cards.note: Hold it until they have it. When they say thanks, say you are welcome.

cards.q: Someone is ahead of you in line. What do you do?
cards.note: Hands to yourself, feet still, and your turn will come.

cards.q: You open a gift and it is a toy you already have. What do you say?
cards.note: Someone picked it just for you. Thank them for thinking of you.

cards.q: A neighbor says, good morning! What do you say back?
cards.note: Look at the person and use a clear voice. A wave works too.

cards.q: What kind of voice do you use in the library?
cards.note: An inside voice is for inside. Save the big voice for the playground.

cards.q: You spill juice on a friend's drawing. After you say sorry, what can you do?
cards.note: Sorry plus helping makes it right.

cards.q: You want some milk. What is the polite way to ask?
cards.note: May I have milk, please? Please and thank you turn a grab into a kind ask.
